# STROBE Statement — checklist of items for cross-sectional studies

| Item | Recommendation | Location in manuscript |
|------|----------------|------------------------|
| 1a Title | Indicate study design | Title: dual-survey secondary analysis of STEPS and DHS |
| 1b Abstract | Informative abstract | Structured abstract |
| 2 Background | Scientific background | Background |
| 3 Objectives | State objectives | End of Background |
| 4 Study design | Present key design elements | Methods — Study design |
| 5 Setting | Settings, locations, dates | Methods — Data sources (STEPS 2015; KDHS 2022) |
| 6 Participants | Eligibility criteria | Methods — age ranges; usual survey eligibility |
| 7 Variables | Outcomes, exposures, predictors | Methods — Outcome definitions |
| 8 Data sources | Measurement details | Methods — STEPS BP/glucose; DHS self-report; PR insurance |
| 9 Bias | Address potential bias | Discussion — Limitations (year gap, age ceilings, constructs) |
| 10 Study size | Explain study size | Results — n=4,500 STEPS; n=40,636 DHS |
| 11 Quantitative variables | Explain handling | Methods — thresholds; cascade stages |
| 12a Statistical methods | Describe methods | Methods — design-based estimators; Erreygers CI |
| 12b Subgroups | Describe | Sex, residence, education; insurance-stratified treatment |
| 12c Missing data | Describe | Domain complete-case restriction |
| 13a Participants | Numbers | Results tables (unweighted n) |
| 14a Descriptive | Characteristics | Table 1; sample composition |
| 15 Outcome data | Report numbers | Tables 1–5 |
| 16 Main results | Estimates and precision | 95% CIs throughout |
| 17 Other analyses | Sensitivity | Table 5 hybrid sensitivity grid |
| 18 Key results | Summarise | Discussion — Principal findings |
| 19 Limitations | Discuss | Discussion — Strengths and limitations |
| 20 Interpretation | Cautious overall | Discussion — Policy implications |
| 21 Generalisability | Discuss | National Kenyan adults; pre-SHA frame |
| 22 Funding | Give sources | Declarations — none specific |
